title: Instrumentation greaseboard — standup capture
content:
Standup: Instrumentation greaseboard — 2027-10-27 (10:15am PT)
Owners: Asha (notes), Marcus (frontend), Diego (backend telemetry), Rina (analytics), Samir (rollouts)
Attendees: Asha, Marcus, Diego, Rina, Samir, + 2 async replies in thread

Purpose: quick sync to triage canary signals, capture low-latency telemetry anomalies, and queue action items for the UI rollouts sprint. This doc is intentionally terse — capture raw observations + follow-ups.

---
HIGHLIGHTS / TL;DR
- Canary for panel-release-3.4 showed a subtle drop in success-rate for panel interactions when TTL cache hits < 60%. (See probe samples below).
- Frontend error rate spike (~0.8% -> 2.6%) correlated with a change in the feature-flag hydration path (PR 1427). Marcus reverted a part of the hydration change; errors dropped to ~1.1% in 20m.
- Analytics ingestion lag increased by ~6m for ingestion-tier-2; Rina suspects backpressure from the new route-level telemetry tags (ENG-4120).
- CI flakiness on smoke tests continues on macos-latest runner; retry temporarily enabled in pipeline.

---
DETAILED NOTES
1) Canary signal details
   - Canary: panel-release-3.4 (10% traffic to canary, US-west region)
   - Symptom: small but reproducible increase in "panel-interaction.failure" where backend returned 500 on lead-edge requests.
   - Probe samples: (sidecar telemetry snapshot)
     - sample A: cache_hit=true, latency=42ms, error=false
     - sample B: cache_hit=false, latency=216ms, error=true, backend_trace=ENG-3862
     - sample C: cache_hit=false, latency=198ms, error=true
   - Hypothesis: when prefix cache misses combine with a cold KV lookup + routing to lower-capacity instance, request hits a timeout boundary (300ms) in the sidecar -> counts as failure.
   - Quick mitigation: increase local sidecar timeout to 500ms for canary nodes only; Diego to roll this as a canary-only patch and monitor.

2) Frontend errors + hydration path
   - PR referenced: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1427 (hydration refactor)
   - Observed: hydration race where flags were read before feature flag store finished initializing, causing undefined state to be read by analytics instrumentation -> null pointer in event builder.
   - Marcus action: revert guardless reads (rolled back 10:30am); will add a guarded init + backoff.
   - Outstanding: add unit + e2e tests around hydration (Samir suggested a lightweight harness that can run in CI to emulate slow KVS).

3) Analytics pipeline backlog
   - Rina: ingestion-tier-2 lag up ~6 minutes; backlog size +2k events. Initial flamegraph shows spend in de-dup + route-tag enrichment.
   - Root cause (suspected): the new route-level tags require a lookup to the routing cache (added in ENG-4120) which is slower than the previous inline tag generation.
   - Short-term: Rina to add a caching layer within the enrichment worker (ttl=30s) to reduce repeated lookups.
   - Long-term: revisit tag design to avoid synchronous enrichments during ingestion path.

4) CI / release pipeline
   - macos-latest flakiness: unrelated to the above but blocking release gating; flaky test is `panel-ux-smoke.test.ts` on macos. Repro steps: flaky selector timingouts when run under heavy host load.
   - Temporary: pipeline increased retry to 2 for macos job; FIXME to investigate flakey test scope.

5) Observability + dashboards
   - Diego: added a temporary heatmap widget to the console-rollouts dashboard that surfaces cache_hit ratio vs panel-error-rate. Link: confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Console+Telemetry+Gallery (notes + screenshots in linked confluence).
   - We agreed to add a kanban card to track adding structured logs for sidecar timeouts (so we can filter by timeout reason).

---
DECISIONS
- Increase canary sidecar timeout to 500ms (canary-only) — Diego (target: 2027-10-27 16:00PT).
- Revert hydration guard changes; add guarded init and test coverage before re-landing — Marcus (wip).
- Add short-term in-memory cache for route tag enrichment in analytics worker — Rina (PR by 2027-10-29).

---
ACTION ITEMS (owner, due)
- Diego: roll canary-sidecar-timeout patch (canary nodes only), watch failure rate -> due 2027-10-27 EOD.
- Marcus: implement guarded hydration + add unit tests + e2e harness design doc -> due 2027-10-29.
- Rina: submit PR with route-tag in-memory cache + perf numbers -> due 2027-10-29.
- Samir: create CI ticket to isolate macos flaky test and add infra trace logs -> ENG-4209 (due 2027-11-03).
- Asha: consolidate this standup capture into the weekly roundup and flag to product for release risk assessment -> due 2027-10-28.

---
NOTES TO SELF / RAW IDEAS (informal)
- consider a "probe-to-key" metric: how many requests require a cold routing lookup vs hit a fast local mapping. Could be helpful to quantify the threshold where cache misses blow up latency.
- experiment: sample 1% of requests and capture full sidecar trace for 5m after each rollout change. Keep traces anonymized.
- follow-up: ask infra if any node rebalancing happened in US-west 10/27 09:50-10:05 (logs show slight node churn).

---
OPEN QUESTIONS
- Is the 300ms timeout in the sidecar a historical artifact from the old runtime? (Diego to check commit history)
- Can we get a safe canary-only config path in the autoscaler to increase instance core limits during experimental rollouts? (Samir to coordinate with infra)
- Is there a feasible async enrichment path for route tags without increasing ingestion latency? (Rina to prototype)

---
ASYNC FOLLOW-UPS (from thread)
- Marcus: posted a short patch that adds a feature-flag init guard; waiting on reviews from Diego + Rina. (PR 1431)
- Rina: uploaded a flamegraph and sample traces to the confluence page; flagged a possible duplicate enrichment call.
- Diego: will attach sidecar debug logs to ENG-3862 and add structured error codes.

---
END / quick capture
This is a working capture. Will iterate and put summary into the weekly console-tooling roundup. If anything critical appears overnight, ping #console-rollouts on Slack and tag @Asha.
